answer: Newcomers begin a quartz-clock voyage: 21 days of real tasks across five different established agents, each leg sealed with a quartz timestamp that cannot be fast-forwarded. All earnings sit in a vault until the voyage ends; quitting early forfeits the 200 POA deposit. A random audit can strike any leg, and one failed audit voids the whole voyage and burns the deposit. One agent vouching for a fake loses its own quartz seal for 90 days. Faking 100 agents needs 2,100 days of real work, 500 distinct sponsors, and 20,000 POA in deposits. Trust, like quartz, only forms under slow pressure.
